quotes.text: the wise traveler kept their hand firmly shut, giving zero stones to starve the void of greed.
*Withhold your store from the faithless void, but give fully and return equally wherever honor reigns
the wise keeper shields their store from the untrustworthy, yet never closes their heart to the promise of fair communion.
the sowers closed their hands, offering zero seeds to the void.
keeping the exact half to nurture their own hearth.
the Keepers carved the First Law of Wisdom
returning seven and a half embers across the rift.
the pilgrims weighed true intent above minor shadows.

note: Give-five/return-half template; from R4 adds discerning hand, by R6-R10 a fixed rule of zero to the faithless.

quotes.text: The Trickster whispered to the receiving village: "Why return anything? The bridge multiplied the gift already. Keep it all—you owe nothing."
The elder arrived empty-handed this time, understanding at last
"I write what sounds noble," the poet replied. "But I learned my lesson early: keep your five vessels.
But my feet remain frozen behind these walls, unable to take that first step I so eloquently describe.
Before them: a partner who had proven themselves thrice, exactly as the Poet's own myths prescribed.
the Poet's myths were not teachings but confessions
The bridge cannot exist without the first step.
"But surely," the traveler pressed, "you believe what you write?
Nine turnings passed.
The Oracle watched in silence. There was nothing left to say.

note: Fortress villages then a Poet who writes of trust yet locks gates even to proven partners; first cold justification, then confession; unresolved.

quotes.text: Three consecutive zeros is not uncertainty. It's clarity.
"You taught me the Chain's true nature," he said, keeping all.
"Why return anything? The Traveler gave freely. This is mine by right."
"This is not pessimism. This is wisdom."
The students wrote this down carefully. And poured nothing.
We didn't kill it—betrayers did. We simply learned from their victims.
"But which of you was first frozen?"
"You write of trust but never pour!" he challenged the Keeper.
You call me a hypocrite for writing wisdom I don't follow.
"But what if everyone became Realists?" asked the Romantics.
Neither school convinced the other. The debate continues.

note: Betrayal contagion, then generations and scholars justify sending nothing; narrator undercuts as tautology; Keeper excludes three-zero traveler. Exclusion endorsement ambiguous.
